issues.legal_issue: An assessing officer may reassess agricultural income that was included in a return but left untaxed as exempt, even when the officer had considered the item in the original assessment.
material_facts: The assessee included the lease-related amount in the agricultural-income return.
The assessing officer considered the item and treated it as exempt from tax in the original assessment.
The same officer later considered the income to have escaped assessment, issued a notice, and made a supplementary assessment.
The issue reached the court in a tax assessment reference and appeal.
issues.conclusion: The assessing officer had jurisdiction to reassess the item under section 26 of the Bihar Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1938.
issues.legal_principle: Section 26 applies where chargeable agricultural income has escaped assessment for any reason; the words “for any reason” are broad enough to cover income returned but erroneously left untaxed as exempt, including where the assessing officer changes the earlier determination. The court applied Kamal Singh v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa, and distinguished Messrs. Chatturam Horilram Ltd. v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Bihar & Orissa. Section 26 was wider in this respect than the then section 34 of the Indian Income-tax Act, which contained conditions not present in section 26.

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_reassessment: The proceeding concerns reassessment of agricultural income for tax purposes.
predicates.returned_income_left_untaxed_as_exempt: The taxpayer included an income item in the return, but the assessing officer left it untaxed on the view that it was exempt.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income tax reassessment concerns income returned but left untaxed as exempt, the assessing officer may reassess that income.

issues.legal_issue: Income derived from agricultural land held under a lease is taxable as agricultural income where the recipient fails to establish that the arrangement was a money-lending transaction and the payment was a repayable loan rather than a lease premium.
material_facts: The assessee held agricultural properties under lease indentures and received income from those properties during the lease terms.

The indentures provided for possession for fixed terms in consideration of payments and reserved annual rent, but did not expressly provide for repayment of a loan, interest, a right of redemption, or personal liability for an outstanding balance.
The assessee claimed that the payment to the lessor was a loan and that the receipts were a capital return from money-lending.

The court found that the assessee had not proved the asserted loan or money-lending character of the transaction, and the agricultural character of the income derived from the land was not seriously contested.
issues.conclusion: The lease income was agricultural income liable to tax, irrespective of the character of the recipient.
issues.legal_principle: Income actually derived from agricultural land is agricultural income and is taxable under the Bihar Agricultural Income-tax Act, 1938, where the asserted money-lending transaction and loan are not proved. In determining whether a zarpeshgi arrangement is a lease or a lease coupled with a mortgage, the court referred to the tests discussed in Mulla’s Transfer of Property Act, 4th edition, page 352, including whether repayment, interest, redemption, or personal liability is provided for.

predicates.leasehold_agricultural_income_tax_assess: The proceeding concerns the tax treatment of income received by a holder of leased agricultural property.
predicates.income_derived_from_agricultural_land: The income received by the leaseholder was derived from agricultural land.
predicates.repayable_loan_proved: The recipient established that the payment to the lessor was a repayable loan rather than a lease premium.

issues.definition: When a leaseholder’s income is derived from agricultural land and the recipient has not proved a repayable loan, the income is taxable as agricultural income regardless of the recipient’s character.
